text: After this, the word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision: "Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield; your reward will be very great."
But Abram said, "Lord GOD, what will you give me? I remain childless, and the one who will inherit my house is Eliezer of Damascus."
Abram said, "Look, you have given me no offspring, so a member of my household will be my heir."
Then the word of the LORD came to him: "He will not be your heir. Your heir will be one who comes from your own body."
He brought him outside and said, "Look up at the sky and count the stars—if you can count them." Then he said to him, "So shall your offspring be."
And Abram believed the LORD, and he credited it to him as righteousness.
He said to him, "I am the LORD, who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans to give you this land to possess."
But Abram said, "Lord GOD, how can I know that I will possess it?"
He answered him, "Take for me a three-year-old heifer, a three-year-old female goat, a three-year-old ram, along with a turtledove and a young pigeon."

versions.text: He answered him, "Bring me a three-year-old heifer, a three-year-old goat, a three-year-old ram, along with a dove and a young pigeon."
versions.explanation: תֹּר designates specifically a turtledove, distinct from the young pigeon (גּוֹזָל); rendering it simply "dove" blurs the pair. Also עֵז is a female goat, matching the feminine forms in the list.

versions.text: He answered him, "Bring me a three-year-old heifer, a three-year-old female goat, a three-year-old ram, along with a turtledove and a young pigeon."
versions.explanation: The verb is לקח, "take," the same root that verse 10 was deliberately revised to render as "took." "Bring me" introduces a different verb idea and breaks the deliberate command-and-fulfillment echo between verses 9 and 10.

text: So Abram took all these, cut them in two, and laid each half opposite the other; but the birds he did not cut in two.

versions.text: So he brought him all these, cut them in two, and laid each half opposite the other; but he did not cut the birds in two.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb is לקח, "took" (for himself), not "brought." As written, "he brought him all these" is also confusing about who is acting; naming Abram clarifies the subject and reads better aloud.

text: Birds of prey came down on the carcasses, but Abram drove them away.
As the sun was setting, a deep sleep fell upon Abram, and suddenly a terror, a great darkness, fell upon him.

versions.text: As the sun was setting, a deep sleep fell upon Abram, and a dreadful darkness came over him.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has three terms—terror, darkness, and great (גְדֹלָה)—and repeats the verb "fall" (נֹפֶלֶת) for dramatic effect. The current rendering drops "great" and weakens the imagery to "came over."

versions.text: As the sun was setting, a deep sleep fell upon Abram, and a great and dreadful darkness fell upon him.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has אֵימָה as a noun ("terror, dread") standing alongside "great darkness," and it opens with וְהִנֵּה, which heightens the drama. Rendering אֵימָה as the mere adjective "dreadful" and omitting וְהִנֵּה flattens the clause; keeping "terror" as a noun and adding "suddenly" preserves both the three terms and the vividness for oral reading.

text: Then the LORD said to Abram, "Know this for certain: your offspring will be strangers in a land not their own, where they will be enslaved and oppressed for four hundred years.
But I will judge the nation they serve, and afterward they will come out with great wealth.
As for you, you will go to your fathers in peace and be buried at a good old age.
In the fourth generation your descendants will return here, for the sin of the Amorites has not yet reached its full measure."
When the sun had set and darkness had fallen, a smoking firepot with a blazing torch appeared and passed between the pieces.
On that day the LORD made a covenant with Abram, saying: "To your offspring I have given this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the Euphrates—
the land of the Kenites, the Kenizzites, the Kadmonites,
the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Rephaim,
the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites, and the Jebusites."
